thread:
lee: Heads-up — I'm thinking about a small canary/observability probe for automatic fallback behavior. Goal: lightweight sampling so we can audit why traffic fell back without flipping the whole route to debug mode.

sam: +1. Are you imagining request-level traces or just a sampled payload snapshot?

lee: sampled payload + routing decision breadcrumb. low retention (30d) and a tamper-proof id to tie to rollout events.

maya: to add — we should tag the sample with the rollout id + rule that triggered fallback. That lets console filter by rollout.

anjali: privacy flag: any sampled payloads must be redacted by default. we can include heuristics and a checkbox to keep raw on for security-reviewed sessions only. also check KMS for linking.

jorge: cost note — full payload sampling at high rates will blow egress and storage. prefer a two-tier sample: 1) small header-only sample for high-rate (essential fields + decision), 2) full payload sample at <0.1% or on-demand.

lee: agree on two-tier. header-only should include: route, model-variant, fallback-reason, rollout-id, sample-id. full payload only when `X-Redwood-Fallback-Sample: full` present.

tess: could we add a "probe" mode in the console that simulates fallback without actually routing? i.e., dry-run sampler so engineers can preview what would have been captured.

sam: probe mode = :100: useful. Also want an API flag so e2e tests can assert sampling behavior. maybe `?fallback_probe=true` or an `X-` header.

devex: for SDKs we can add `client.addFallbackSampleId()` helper and doc snippet. add short code example and an example header:```
X-Redwood-Fallback-Sample: canary-20260402-abc123
Fallback-Probe: true
```

lee: nice. console UI: add a small "sample stream" panel under Rollouts -> Canary where you can watch sampled breadcrumbs in near real-time (low rate) and request full payload on demand with audit annotation.

maya: telemetry: emit metric `rollout.fallback.sampled_total` and histogram `fallback.latency_by_reason`. also attach `sample_id` as tag for debug joins.

jorge: build side — we'll need a new sampling service or extend routing-proxy to tag and forward samples to telemetry pipeline. prefer sidecar to avoid p95 perf changes.

anjali: audit chain: every time someone clicks to view a full sample, log `audit.view` with user, reason, and consent checkbox state. essential for compliance.

ops-bot: ALERT: canary fallback observed on route /v1/chat for rollout rlt-2026-04-02 at 2026-04-02T15:22:08Z (reason: model_timeout). sample_id=canary-20260402-abc123

tess: ops-bot alert is useful. can we add a quick link in alerts to "see sample" that opens the console view with filters pre-populated?

lee: yep — link pattern `https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/{rollout-id}/samples?sample_id={id}`. will add route.

sam: question about retention/TTL config: should this be per-rollout or org-level? my vote: org-level default + rollout override. small teams use defaults, platform & enterprise can override.

maya: agreed. defaults: header-only 90d? wait we said 30d earlier. prefer header-only 90d, full payload 30d. and ROI override for enterprise.

lee: decision checklist so far: 1) implement two-tier sampling (header-only + full on demand) 2) add probe/dry-run mode 3) header format `X-Redwood-Fallback-Sample` + `Fallback-Probe` flag 4) metrics + sample_id tag 5) audit log for full sample access 6) console sample stream + quick-link from alerts 7) org-default retention with rollout override.

sam: re: API — also add rate-limited toggle `sampling.push=true` that operator teams can turn off during incidents.

jorge: infra tasks: prototype in routing-proxy sidecar, publish sample headers to kafka topic `fallback-samples.v1` with header-only payload by default. full payload push requires `sample:full` event to be emitted.

devex: I'll draft a quick docs PR and sample code snippets. want to include a note about redaction + compliance.

anjali: I'll write the audit requirements and consent flow. coordinate with legal before we enable full payload retention by default for any customer.

lee: timeline? can someone prototype a mock in staging this sprint?

jorge: I can spike it — small sidecar change + kafka topic. will push a demo by Thu.

tess: I'll mock up the sample-stream UI and the alert quick-link tomorrow.

sam: I'll add API header support in SDKs and tests.

lee: awesome — thanks. one last ask: keep the UX minimal. the default console views should not expose raw payloads unless you explicitly opt in.

maya: noted. privacy-forward by default.

lee: ok we'll sync Thu standup. if anyone wants to take an action item, drop it here. :white_check_mark:
